# Technology Strategy, Execution & Governance — Alexandro Sances

> Independent professional reference repository containing technology strategy and governance frameworks, enterprise AI and RAG governance guidance, digital portfolio governance, open-source strategy, digital infrastructure and sustainability frameworks, executive playbooks and practical templates.

This repository explains how organisations connect strategic outcomes to technology choices, investment decisions, governance, delivery, adoption and measurable benefits. It is technology-neutral: specialist frameworks address domain-specific risks without creating disconnected governance systems.

## Start here

- [Main repository guide](README.md): overview, getting started, governance model, domains and author context.
- [Frameworks index](frameworks/README.md): map of the reference frameworks and how they relate.
- [Templates index](templates/README.md): catalogue and practical sequence for using the operational tools.

## Core governance frameworks

- [Technology Strategy & Execution Governance Framework](frameworks/technology-strategy-execution-governance.md): connects strategic outcomes, capabilities, technology choices, investment, delivery and benefits.
- [Strategy & Execution Governance — Executive Playbook](frameworks/strategy-execution-governance-playbook.md): operating method for decision rights, prioritisation, mandate, steering, escalation and benefits.
- [Digital Portfolio Governance Framework](frameworks/digital-portfolio-governance.md): portfolio selection, capacity, dependencies, sequencing and rebalancing.

## Strategic technology domains

- [Enterprise AI & RAG Governance Blueprint](frameworks/enterprise-ai-rag-governance-blueprint.md): information readiness, source governance, access control, evaluation, human oversight and lifecycle risk.
- [Open Source Strategy & Governance](frameworks/open-source-strategy-governance.md): ecosystem health, dependency management, licensing, supply-chain transparency, stewardship, contribution and exit.
- [Digital Sustainability and Data Centre Energy Governance](frameworks/digital-sustainability-data-centre-governance.md): service demand, infrastructure capacity, energy, water, resilience and lifecycle economics.

## Operational templates and examples

- [Initiative Canvas](templates/initiative-canvas.md): initiative framing, outcomes, options, ownership, dependencies and requested decision.
- [Weighted Scoring Matrix](templates/weighted-scoring-matrix.md): comparison of discretionary options; mandatory obligations are handled separately.
- [Decision Record](templates/decision-record.md): record of rationale, authority, conditions, actions and review triggers.
- [Governance Forums](templates/governance-forums.md): forum remits, decision classes, charters and escalation paths.
- [AI/RAG Use-Case Assessment](templates/ai-rag-use-case-assessment.md): use-case suitability, information sources, threat modelling and evaluation.
- [Open-Source Assessment](templates/open-source-assessment.md): option assessment, governance health, participation and exit readiness.
- [Infrastructure Capacity Decision](templates/infrastructure-capacity-decision.md): capacity options, measurement boundaries and infrastructure decision gates.
- [Benefit Profile](templates/benefit-profile.md): baseline, target, ownership, attribution and review of benefits.
- [Strategic Dependency Register](templates/strategic-dependency-register.md): visibility of cross-initiative dependencies, owners and responses.
- [Initiative Canvas — Fictional Worked Example](templates/initiative-canvas-example.md): completed illustrative scenario; all organisations, assumptions and values are fictional.
- [Decision Record — Fictional Worked Example](templates/decision-record-example.md): illustrative decision record; not an actual organisational decision.

## How to interpret the material

- Frameworks describe governance principles and operating models; templates are adaptable working artefacts.
- Worked examples are fictional illustrations, not evidence of actual implementations, decisions, measured performance or achieved results.
- Scores, thresholds, estimates and targets must be validated in the user's organisational context.
- The material is independent professional guidance, not legal, financial, security, procurement or regulatory advice.
- The views and materials are personal and do not necessarily represent any organisation with which the author is or has been associated.
